purpose: 三人合為同一透明圖層，先確認群像摹繪再製作動畫
prompt:
Use case: historical-scene / compositing.
Asset: ONE unified transparent-background master drawing of a THREE-PERSON Chinese painting ensemble, to be approved BEFORE any animation.
The input is the sole original painting reference. Redraw the three musicians together as a single coherent painted group element, including all their original instruments and the foreground drum/stool. This is a careful tracing/repainting, not a modern redesign or separate pasted cutouts.

Characters and fixed relationships:
- foreground seated brown/ochre-robed elderly drummer, original small moustache/beard, dark cap with thin red edge, white cuffs and waist cloth, legs and robe in the same seated silhouette; both hands holding the two original thin drumsticks in the original low resting pose.
- blue-robed cymbal player standing immediately BEHIND the drummer, original cap, small face, two large brass cymbals in their original overlapping positions. Keep the cymbals behind the drummer's head where the original overlaps.
- grey-robed musician on the RIGHT, original dark vest and red-topped cap, holding the original small suspended gong and beater in the original posture. His body is partly hidden by the large foreground drum.
- include the large barrel drum, full drumhead, body/ropes and stand/feet, plus the small stool below the seated drummer, exactly in the reference proportions.
Keep all three people's positions, proportions, scale relative to each other, facing directions, original facial identities, clothing folds and front-to-back overlaps faithfully. Keep original occlusion: do not invent visible hidden legs, extra hands, additional instruments or uncovered body parts.

STYLE: one consistent hand-painted old Chinese handscroll style. Fine subdued ink lines, faded mineral/earth colors, mottled/worn silk-like pigment texture INSIDE the painted people and objects, softly painted small faces. Match the original muted blue, olive-ochre/brown, grey and aged brass. No crisp modern cartoon outlines, digital vector look, 3D, photorealistic skin, vibrant color or glossy/clean new costumes. The entire three-person group must feel painted together by the same brush.

COMPOSITION: single portrait canvas at the original 240:295 aspect ratio. Preserve the original coordinate positions/framing; do not recenter the individual figures. Leave a small transparent outer margin so every instrument, sleeve, robe, stool and drum foot is intact. Exactly ONE group, not a sheet, not separate panels, no duplicated people, no alternative poses.

BACKGROUND: TRUE alpha transparency, including holes between people, instrument handles, stool legs and empty space around the group. REMOVE ALL architecture, curtain, wall, floor, threshold, plants, hanging decorations, the red guard at extreme left and the partial horn player at extreme right. NO rectangular paper patch, no painted wall behind them, no checkerboard baked into the image, no white/beige fill, no ground plane or drop shadow. The texture belongs only inside the painted group itself. No labels, text, borders, guides or graphics. This should be a complete usable group illustration master, from which an animation can later be drawn coherently.
correctionPrompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Correct ONE composition issue in the transparent group drawing (image 1), using the original scene (image 2) as position reference.
Keep image 1's unified hand-painted style, muted palette, worn pigment texture, faces, three-person cast, instruments and TRUE alpha background. Do not add any scene/background.

The FOREGROUND BROWN DRUMMER is too far to the right relative to the blue musician. In the original, the brown drummer's head is slightly LEFT of the blue musician's head. In image1 it is clearly RIGHT.
Move the brown drummer's head, neck, shoulders, seated torso and lower robe approximately 7 percent of the full canvas width to the LEFT, keeping him seated on the same stool. Adjust his seated body and stool placement coherently as needed, without clipping the stool legs. His two hands must remain naturally near the left side of the drumhead in their low resting pose, each gripping its thin straight drumstick; redraw connected sleeves/elbows to accommodate the corrected torso position. Do not merely shift a cutout or stretch pixels.
DO NOT move the blue cymbal player, grey gong player or large barrel drum. Keep their current exact sizes and positions. Preserve the cymbals BEHIND the drummer's head and the complete front-to-back overlap. Do not change facial identity, expression, costumes or brushwork. Retain original occlusion of hidden legs.
Keep every part inside the canvas with a transparent margin. Preserve alpha transparency including stool gaps, inter-person gaps, gong strap hole; no black/white/beige fill or paper rectangle, no floor, shadow, architecture or text. Exactly one unified painted group, no panels or duplicates.
alpha: Original generated RGBA preserved. Image size 1131x1391. Alpha extrema 0..255; visible bounds at alpha>32: [75,80,1102,1313].
status: Unified master produced before whole-group animation; see animation-generation.json for the current sample. Previous layered group rig is unmounted.
